**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, confidence 0.90).**

**What the document does:**
- **p0149 (§ General Provisions (c) ASSIGNMENT):** blanket prohibition on any Licensee assignment, sublicense or transfer without Licensor's prior written consent — no affiliate carve-out, no M&A/successor carve-out, no reasonableness standard, and no reciprocal restriction on Licensor (Licensor is free to assign, including to our competitors).
- **p0134 (Article XX):** on any Change of Control of Licensee (defined at p0135 to include asset sale, merger, or majority equity transfer), the Agreement and *all* Licensee licenses **automatically terminate** unless Licensor consented in advance; Licensor is deemed reasonable in refusing if it merely "believes its interests will be adversely effected."
- Aggravated by the Article XXII right of first refusal over our M&A transactions (p0139), noted but not separately redlined under this rule.

Both features sit in walk-away territory under ASSIGN, so this fails the fallback, not just the preferred position.

**Redline (validated ok:true):**
1. p0149 — Licensee may assign without consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all/substantially all assets or equity; residual consent requirement made mutual and "not unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned"; Licensor barred from assigning to a Licensee competitor.
2. p0134 — automatic change-of-control termination replaced with a confirmation that a Change of Control gives Licensor no termination, suspension or re-pricing right, plus a 30-day post-closing notice obligation on us (the "Change of Control" definition is left intact so the cross-reference in p0149 still works).

The comment offers the fallback (mutual assignment to successors on written notice) as a negotiating position.
